title: Embedded Reliability Coach - Micro SLO Pilot
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes a 10-week pilot to embed a Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) as a reliability coach inside 3 product feature teams to trial a ‘micro-SLO’ pattern. The goal is to validate whether short-lived, narrowly scoped SLOs plus hands-on coaching can accelerate SLO adoption, reduce incident-to-resolution time, and create reproducible playbooks that scale across the org.

Context and hypothesis:
- Problem: Many feature teams are hesitant to adopt full-service-level SLOs because defining, measuring, and operationalizing them feels heavyweight and brittle.
- Hypothesis: If a lightweight SRE coach partners with a team to define a micro-SLO (one objective, simple metric, short evaluation window), then teams will adopt SLO-guided decision-making faster than standard SLO onboarding.
- Success metrics (pilot-level):
  - 3 teams have active micro-SLOs instrumented and visualized in the console within 6 weeks.
  - Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for incidents relating to pilot SLOs reduced by 30% vs baseline.
  - At least 2 teams retain or expand micro-SLOs at pilot end.

Scope and constraints:
- Micro-SLO definition: single metric (latency or availability), narrow user impact slice (e.g., web->API flow for search), short lookback (7-day burn rate).
- Not in scope: org-wide SLI catalog changes, infra-level kernel changes, major library rewrites.
- Pilot timeframe: 2025-10-20 -> 2026-01-02 (10 weeks + 1 retro).

Teams selected (initial):
1) Search UX (team lead: Jonah Rivera) — candidate SLO: p95 latency for search responses for signed-in users < 350ms (7d burn).
2) Chat Routing (team lead: Priya Singh) — candidate SLO: error rate on request routing < 0.35% (7d burn).
3) Embeddings API (team lead: Asha Patel) — candidate SLO: provisioning availability of embeddings model pool >= 99.8% (7d burn).

Coach/resourcing model:
- Embedded coach: Maya Chen (primary), 0.6 FTE per team initially (rotating weekly office hours + 1:1 pairing twice a week).
- Backup coach: Liam O'Connor (on-call for escalation and tooling help).
- Platform support: Observability infra will provision dashboards, alerts, and pre-built SLI collectors (task SRE-1182).

Pilot plan and weekly cadence (10 weeks):
- Week 0 (preparation, 1 week): identify teams, confirm owners, baseline measurement, grant dashboard access.
- Weeks 1-2 (define & instrument): coach + team define micro-SLO, select SLI, set alert thresholds, instrument metrics. Deliverable: dashboard + test alert.
- Weeks 3-5 (observe & iterate): run with shadow alerts (no paging), refine SLI tagging and thresholds. Deliverable: first 7-day burn report.
- Weeks 6-7 (operate & escalate): enable paging/rotation for SLO alerts, practice incident playbook with simulated degradations. Deliverable: incident playbook + runbook entry.
- Weeks 8-9 (stabilize & evaluate): collect metrics for success criteria, survey team sentiment, capture lessons.
- Week 10 (scale decision & retro): decide adoption path (retain/expand/terminate), produce final artifacts: templates, onboarding checklist, measurement dashboard, and training materials.

Experiment matrix (per team):
- Metric type: latency vs availability vs error rate.
- Granularity: global vs user-segment vs route.
- Alert policy: shadow-only vs paging with 15/60/240 minute thresholds.
- Remediation approach: auto-rollback toggle vs ops runbook vs cache purge.
We will run one orthogonal variation per team to learn trade-offs.

Definition of success (team-level):
- Instrumentation: SLI, dashboard, and one alert channel created and validated.
- Behavioral change: team includes SLO status in weekly planning and on-call triage.
- Reliability outcome: meaningful reduction in incident frequency or severity for the scoped surface area (compare prior 8 weeks baseline).

Observation, measurement, and dashboards:
- Baseline collection (pre-pilot): 8 weeks of current telemetry for chosen metric.
- Burn-rate visualization: 7d and 30d burn windows; annotate deploys and config changes.
- Cost tracking: token and GPU impact of any new instrumentation (avoid high-cardinality SLIs).
- Source of truth dashboards: per-team SLO panel in Redwood Console + an aggregated pilot board.

Operational playbooks / runbooks to produce:
- Onboarding checklist for new micro-SLOs (permissions, labels, alerting channels).
- Incident playbook with clear escalation, owner, mitigation steps, and rollback triggers.
- Postmortem template specific to micro-SLO failure modes.

Training and knowledge transfer:
- Week 2 lunch-and-learn: how to pick a micro-SLO and write a useful SLI.
- Pairing sessions: coach pairs with on-call engineer during 2 real incidents (or simulated).
- Office hours: weekly 1-hour open drop-in on Thursdays #sre-embedded-coach.

Communication plan:
- Weekly status note posted to Confluence + summarized in #sre-embedded-coach.
- Biweekly sync with product leadership for product risk and rollout decisions.
- All postmortems and runbooks linked into the project Confluence page.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Teams treat micro-SLO as checkbox. Mitigation: coach enforces review of SLO at planning meeting for 4 weeks.
- Risk: Alert noise leads to alert fatigue. Mitigation: start with shadow alerts and calibrate thresholds before paging.
- Risk: High-cardinality SLIs increase ingestion cost. Mitigation: restrict SLI cardinality and prefer sampled traces for drill-down.

Artifacts to deliver at pilot end:
- Standardized micro-SLO template (YAML + human-readable summary).
- Onboarding checklist and CI pipeline snippet for metric instrumentation.
- Two short training videos (how-to create a micro-SLO; how to run a micro-SLO postmortem).
- Pilot retrospective with recommended adoption play (scale plan).

Next steps (immediate):
1) Confirm team participation and sign-off by 2025-10-16 (owners: Jonah, Priya, Asha).
2) Observability infra to provision pilot dashboards and grant access (owner: Liam, due 2025-10-17).
3) Kickoff meeting and baseline capture (Maya to schedule for 2025-10-20).

Open questions (for leadership):
- What allocation of SRE headcount is acceptable if all 3 teams choose to continue?
- Are teams allowed to convert micro-SLOs into product-level SLOs without additional approvals?

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is a working draft intended for the reliability program leadership and the 3 pilot teams. Feedback wanted on the coach cadence, experiment variations, and success criteria.

Appendix (short templates):
- Micro-SLO one-liner: <metric> for <user-slice> should be <objective> (window: 7d).
- Example: "Search p95 for signed-in users < 350ms (7d)".
- Minimal dashboard items: SLI timeseries, error budget burn rate, recent deploys, top 3 traces by latency.
